meta.title: The IAS machine family, 1946–1960
meta.description: Computers built from, or closely modelled on, the Institute for Advanced Study machine designed under John von Neumann at Princeton, whose drawings were deliberately circulated. Each node is placed where and when the machine first ran. Each link says which design it was copied from.
sources: Wikipedia, 'IAS machine' (list of IAS-derived machines), retrieved 22 Sept 2026
meta.caveats: Years are first-operational years, rounded; several machines ran partially a year before formal completion. BESM is listed among IAS-family machines in some sources but was an independent Soviet design, so its link is marked as inference. SEAC, which also appears in some IAS lists, followed the EDVAC design and is left out. Machines copied directly from the IAS design are linked to the 1946 design reports rather than to the finished machine, since several ran before it did.

nodes.label: IAS design reports
nodes.note: Burks, Goldstine and von Neumann, 'Preliminary Discussion of the Logical Design of an Electronic Computing Instrument' (1946), with the progress reports that followed. They were circulated freely, so the machines below descend from the design as much as from the machine.

nodes.label: IAS machine
nodes.note: The template. Design reports circulated to other groups from 1946.

nodes.label: ORDVAC
nodes.place: Built at Illinois for Aberdeen Proving Ground, Maryland
nodes.note: Built at the University of Illinois from the IAS design and delivered to the Army. It ran before the IAS machine itself was finished.

nodes.label: ILLIAC I
nodes.note: Twin of ORDVAC, kept at Illinois. Operational 1 September 1952.

nodes.label: MANIAC I
nodes.note: Built for weapons calculations.

nodes.label: IBM 701
nodes.note: IBM's first commercial scientific computer, influenced by the IAS design. Nineteen were installed.

nodes.label: JOHNNIAC
nodes.note: Modelled on the IAS machine, with 40-bit words and Selectron memory.

nodes.label: ORACLE
nodes.note: Built at Argonne for Oak Ridge.

nodes.label: BESK
nodes.note: Closely modelled on the IAS machine from drawings obtained in Princeton. Inaugurated 1 April 1954.

nodes.label: BESM
nodes.note: Listed among IAS-family machines in some sources, but an independent design by S. A. Lebedev's group. Its link is inference, not record.

nodes.label: WEIZAC
nodes.note: The first computer in Israel, built from the IAS design.

nodes.label: SILLIAC
nodes.note: The Sydney version of ILLIAC.

nodes.label: SMIL
nodes.note: Highly inspired by BESK.

nodes.label: FACIT EDB
nodes.note: Software-compatible copies of BESK. Nine were built.

nodes.label: SARA
nodes.note: Highly inspired by BESK. Work started in 1955.

nodes.label: MISTIC
nodes.note: Built from the ILLIAC design.

nodes.label: GEORGE
nodes.note: Argonne's successor to AVIDAC.

nodes.label: DASK
nodes.note: Highly inspired by BESK.

nodes.label: CYCLONE
nodes.note: Built from the ILLIAC design.

nodes.label: TIFRAC
nodes.place: Tata Institute of Fundamental Research, Bombay
nodes.note: India's first indigenously built computer, following the IAS design.
